key_insight: PROBE trains LLM-based auditors to discover policy violations in tool-using agents through realistic multi-turn interactions, revealing failures that standard capability and safety benchmarks miss.
engineering_relevance: This matters for deploying agentic systems in high-stakes settings because it provides a scalable way to audit compliance with pricing, privacy, confirmation, and safety policies during actual tool use.
method: Formulate agent auditing as a two-player Markov game between an auditor and a deployed agent.
Train auditors with a composite reward that balances violation discovery, plausibility, progress, and policy diversity.
Compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization for learning effective auditors.
evidence_signal: In extensive experiments, PROBE-trained auditors found broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor was much smaller than the target agent.
watch_item: Because policy violations can emerge only after multiple turns or in downstream systems, auditing quality may depend on realistic environment modeling and careful policy specification.
paper_title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
